vocab.def: A sequence is a function whose domain is either the set of all positive integers or the set of the first m positive integers, for some positive integer m.
A finite sequence is a function u defined on the set M = {1, 2, 3, ..., m}, where m is a positive integer.
vocab.ex:
\[
1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4,\ 5.
\]

This is a finite sequence

vocab.def:
An infinite sequence is a function whose domain is the set of positive integers 
\(\mathbb{N}^*\).
Notation
\[
(u_n):\quad u_1,u_2,u_3,\ldots,u_n,\ldots
\]
vocab.ex: 1, 2, 3, 4, ... is an infinite sequence.

vocab.def: A number in a sequence.
vocab.ex: In 2, 4, 6, the second term is 4.

vocab.def:
\[u_n=f(n),\quad n\in\mathbb N^*
\]
vocab.ex:
\[u_n=2n,\quad n\geq1

\]

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is called an increasing sequence if 
\[
\boxed{u_{n+1}>u_n,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*}
\]
vocab.ex: The sequence \(1,3,5,7,9,\ldots\) is an increasing sequence.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is called a decreasing sequence if
\[
\boxed{u_{n+1}<u_n,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*.}
\]
vocab.ex: The sequence \(10,8,6,4,2,\ldots\) is decreasing.

vocab.def:
\[
u_n=c,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*
\]
vocab.ex: The sequence \(3,3,3,3,\ldots\) is a constant sequence.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is called a bounded sequence if it is both bounded above and bounded below. \[
\boxed{\exists\,m,M:
m\le u_n\le M,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*.}
\]
vocab.ex:
\[
0<u_n=\frac1n\le1\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*,
\]The sequence \((u_n)\) is bounded.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is said to be bounded above if there exists a real number \(M\) such that \[u_n\le M,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*.
\]
vocab.ex:
\[
u_n=\frac1n\le1,\quad n\in\mathbb N^*
\]

The sequence is bounded above by 1.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is said to be bounded below if there exists a real number \(m\) such that 
\[u_n\ge m,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*.\]
vocab.ex:
\[
u_n=-\frac1n\ge-1,\quad n\in\mathbb N^*
\]

The sequence is bounded below by \(-1\).

vocab.def:
\[u_{n+1}=u_n+d,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*.

\] \(d\) called the common difference.
vocab.ex: The sequence \(2,5,8,11,14,\ldots\) is an arithmetic sequence with first term \(u_1=2\) and common difference \(d=3\).

vocab.def:
The common difference of an arithmetic sequence: \[d=u_{n+1}-u_n,\quad \forall n\in\mathbb N^*.

\]
vocab.ex:
\[
2,\ 5,\ 8,\ 11,\ 14,\ldots
\]

The common difference of this arithmetic sequence is \(d=3\).

vocab.def: The relative position describes how two geometric objects are positioned in relation to each other.
vocab.ex: Two lines in space can be parallel, intersecting, or skew.

vocab.def: Two lines are parallel if they lie in the same plane and do not intersect.
vocab.ex: Lines \(a\) and \(b\) lie in the same plane and do not intersect. Therefore, \(a\parallel b\).

vocab.def: Two lines are intersecting if they have exactly one common point.
vocab.ex: Lines \(a\) and \(b\) intersect at point \(O\).

vocab.def: Two lines are coincident if they have all their points in common.
vocab.ex: Lines \(a\) and \(b\) coincide.

vocab.def: Two lines are skew if they do not lie in the same plane.
vocab.ex: In tetrahedron \(ABCD\), lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) are skew.

vocab.ex: Line \(a\) is parallel to plane \((P)\). Notation: \(a\parallel(P)\).

vocab.def: A line intersects a plane if they have exactly one point in common.

vocab.def: Two distinct planes are parallel if they have no points in common.
vocab.ex: Planes \((P)\) and \((Q)\) have no points in common. Therefore, they are parallel.Notation: \((P)\parallel(Q)\).

vocab.def:
Given a plane \((\alpha)\) and a line \(\Delta\) intersecting \((\alpha)\), for any point \(M\) in space, the line through \(M\) parallel to or coinciding with \(\Delta\) intersects \((\alpha)\) at a unique point \(M'\).

The point \(M'\) is called the parallel projection of \(M\) onto \((\alpha)\) along the direction of \(\Delta\). The mapping that sends each point \(M\) to its corresponding point \(M'\) is called a parallel projection.
vocab.ex: Find “Parallel projection” in an English mathematics question.

vocab.def: The English term for “Phương chiếu” in mathematics.
vocab.ex: In a parallel projection onto plane \((\alpha)\) along direction \(\Delta\), the line \(\Delta\) determines the direction of projection.

vocab.def: The English term for “Mặt phẳng chiếu” in mathematics.
vocab.ex: In a parallel projection onto plane \((\alpha)\) along direction \(\Delta\), plane \((\alpha)\) is the projection plane.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is said to have a limit \(a\) as \(n\to+\infty\) if
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}(u_n-a)=0.
\]

This is denoted by
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}u_n=a
\]

or \(u_n\to a\) as \(n\to+\infty\).
vocab.ex:
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{2n+1}{n}=2
\]

The limit of the sequence \(\displaystyle u_n=\frac{2n+1}{n}\) as \(n\) approaches positive infinity is 2.

vocab.vi: Dãy số có giới hạn bằng 0
vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is said to converge to zero as \(n\) approaches positive infinity if, for any arbitrarily small positive number, \(|u_n|\) is smaller than that number for all sufficiently large values of \(n\).

This is denoted by
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}u_n=0
\]

or \(u_n\to0\) as \(n\to+\infty\).
vocab.ex:
\[
u_n=\frac{1}{n}
\]

\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}\frac{1}{n}=0
\]

The sequence \(\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)\) tends to zero as \(n\) approaches positive infinity.

Dãy số \(\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)\) có giới hạn bằng 0 khi \(n\) tiến tới dương vô cực.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is said to tend to positive infinity as \(n\to+\infty\) if its terms become greater than any given positive number for all sufficiently large values of \(n\).

This is denoted by
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}u_n=+\infty
\]

or \(u_n\to+\infty\) as \(n\to+\infty\).
vocab.ex:
\[
u_n=2n+1
\]

\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}(2n+1)=+\infty
\]

The sequence \((u_n)\) tends to positive infinity as \(n\) approaches positive infinity.

vocab.def:
A sequence \((u_n)\) is said to tend to negative infinity as \(n\to+\infty\) if
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}(-u_n)=+\infty.
\]

This is denoted by
\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}u_n=-\infty
\]

or \(u_n\to-\infty\) as \(n\to+\infty\).
vocab.ex:
\[
u_n=-3n
\]

\[
\lim_{n\to+\infty}(-3n)=-\infty
\]

The sequence \((u_n)\) tends to negative infinity as \(n\) approaches positive infinity.

vocab.en: Sum of an Infinite geometric series
vocab.vi: Tổng của cấp số nhân lùi vô hạn.
vocab.def:
The sum of an infinite geometric series with first term \(u_1\) and common ratio \(q\), where \(|q|<1\), is the limit of the sum of its first \(n\) terms as \(n\) approaches positive infinity.
\[
\boxed{S=\lim_{n\to+\infty}S_n=\frac{u_1}{1-q},\quad |q|<1}
\]
vocab.ex:
\[
1+\frac12+\frac14+\frac18+\cdots=2
\]

The sum of this infinite geometric series is 2.

vocab.def: The English term for “Giới hạn của hàm số” in mathematics.
vocab.ex: Find “Limit of a function” in an English mathematics question.

vocab.def:
Let \((a,b)\) be an open interval containing \(x_0\), and let \(f(x)\) be a function defined on \((a,b)\setminus\{x_0\}\).

The function \(f(x)\) is said to have a limit \(L\) as \(x\) approaches \(x_0\) if, for every sequence \((x_n)\) in \((a,b)\setminus\{x_0\}\) converging to \(x_0\), the sequence \((f(x_n))\) converges to \(L\).

This is denoted by
\[
\boxed{\lim_{x\to x_0}f(x)=L.}
\]

vocab.def:
Let \(f(x)\) be a function defined on the interval \((a,x_0)\). A number \(L\) is called the left-hand limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) approaches \(x_0\) if, for every sequence \((x_n)\) satisfying
\[
a<x_n<x_0,\qquad x_n\to x_0,
\]

we have
\[
f(x_n)\to L.
\]

This is denoted by
\[
\boxed{\lim_{x\to x_0^-}f(x)=L.}
\]
vocab.ex:
Given the function
\[
f(x)=x^2+1,\quad x<2.
\]

We have
\[
\boxed{\lim_{x\to2^-}(x^2+1)=5}
\]

The left-hand limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) approaches 2 is 5.

vocab.def:
Let \(f(x)\) be a function defined on the interval \((x_0,b)\). A number \(L\) is called the right-hand limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) approaches \(x_0\) if, for every sequence \((x_n)\) satisfying
\[
x_0<x_n<b,\qquad x_n\to x_0,
\]

we have
\[
f(x_n)\to L.
\]

This is denoted by
\[
\boxed{\lim_{x\to x_0^+}f(x)=L.}
\]
vocab.ex:
Given the function
\[
f(x)=2x+1,\quad x>1.
\]

We have
\[
\boxed{\lim_{x\to1^+}(2x+1)=3}
\]
